title: Idempotency trace event state
description: Shape of the `state` field for http-idempotency trace events.

base.description: The collection URL this server exposes, e.g. '/orders'.

resources.description: Everything stored on the server right now, one entry per resource.

fields.description: The stored representation, in a stable display order.

mark.description: How the current request touched this resource.

keys.description: The idempotency-key record: what the server stored so it can recognize a retry.

key.description: The Idempotency-Key value the client sent.

path.description: The resource the first call produced.

status.description: The response stored for a replay.

sideEffects.description: Effects outside the stored representation (mails, webhooks, downstream calls), in the order they fired.

request.description: The request being processed (absent before the first one).

attempt.description: How many times this identical request has been sent, starting at 1.

key.description: The Idempotency-Key header, or null when the request carries none.

idempotentBySpec.description: What the HTTP spec promises about repeating this method.

relative.description: Whether the body is a relative operation ('+1') instead of a target value.

body.description: The request body as sent; empty for methods that carry none.

response.description: The answer produced for the current request.

status.description: HTTP status line ('200 OK', '404 Not Found'), or 'pending' while the request is still being processed.

delivered.description: Whether the answer actually reached the client, or was lost on the way back.

replayed.description: Whether the answer was replayed from the idempotency-key record instead of executed.

ledger.description: Every attempt in the order it was sent, with what came of it.

method.description: The HTTP method of this attempt.

attempt.description: How many times this identical request had been sent by then.

key.description: The Idempotency-Key of this attempt, or null.

status.description: The status line the server produced.

delivered.description: Whether the client received the answer.

outcome.description: What this attempt did: applied a change, repeated one harmlessly, duplicated it, leaked a side effect, was replayed from a key, was a safe read, or did nothing.

counters.description: Running totals for the whole run.

lost.description: Answers that never reached the client.

duplicates.description: Repeats that changed something again — the ones that should not have.

replays.description: Repeats recognized by an idempotency key and answered from the record.
